predecessor.frontier_summary: r251 established sequential same-path create-once duplicate rejection after first visibility; true concurrent first-writer behavior remained unresolved.

slice.objective: Test the remaining same-intent concurrency gap with a deterministic two-actor interleaving model over one create-once path, without parallel workers, protected authority, hosted compute, finite quota, or user execution.
slice.candidate: linearizable create-once uniqueness fence keyed by deterministic intent path
model_assumptions: Actors A and B represent two attempts carrying the same deterministic intent_id and targeting the same create-once path.
A provider-observable execution is serialized into one of exactly two first-create orderings: A then B, or B then A.
The first create observed while ABSENT commits exactly one effect and transitions the path to PRESENT(winner, effect_counter=1).

A later create to the same PRESENT path is rejected or otherwise produces no second committed effect unless an explicit update/CAS route is used; this transition is grounded only by r251's sequential same-path GitHub Contents observation.
The model does not assume anything about a provider that is not linearizable for simultaneous first-create requests.

enumerated_orderings.result: A commits effect_counter=1; B observes PRESENT and cannot commit a second create-once effect
B commits effect_counter=1; A observes PRESENT and cannot commit a second create-once effect

slice.exact_tested_scope: Deterministic state-machine proof over the two serialized provider-observable orderings for two same-intent create-once attempts, using r251 only as the sequential transition premise that an already-present path rejects a second create. scope_limits: True simultaneous first-writer arrival before either request observes PRESENT is not experimentally tested.
Provider behavior under network partitions, retries with uncertain acknowledgement, replication lag, or multi-region storage is not established by this model.
This does not prove full richer-mode outcome parity or Phase-1 closure.
slice.semantic_conclusion: Conditional result only: if the create-once path primitive is linearizable for same-path first creation, then every two-actor same-intent ordering commits at most one effect. This closes the serialized interleaving child but leaves the provider linearizability premise and provider-independent durability as unresolved children.
